summary: Gerald D. Jayne, writing on behalf of the Idaho Environmental Council, opposes unregulated ORV use on public lands, arguing that the status quo of nearly unlimited off-road use must be changed before problems worsen. He urges federal land administrators to take bold steps to establish meaningful ORV regulations under Executive Order 11644, rejecting the notion that motorized users have an inherent right to access all public lands. He further argues that federal initiatives should not promote ORV use, that public lands are not playgrounds for machines, and that the trend toward increasing ORV use is socially undesirable and should be reversed.
